_about: One entry per exported method of App (Wails binds them all). Read by bound_methods_test.go: a method with no entry, an entry for a method that does not exist, and an entry that contradicts the code fail the test. callers: window, bridge (the headless HTTP bridge, with its token), automation (the automation endpoint). touches: files, devices, network, keychain. confirm: none; asks (Go itself requires a person's answer in the window, and without a window or an answer the action is not done: no window means no); previewed (Go compares what the call names with what it holds and refuses on a mismatch: a destination label that must still be the current one, a preview id that must exist, a host that must have been checked. For an id or a checked host an earlier preview must have happened, for a destination label only the comparison does. Nothing in Go asks a person, and a script that holds the bridge token can make the preview itself); answers (it is the answer); native-dialog (only a person in a native dialog can drive it). decision: required for an aiProvider or network method with confirm none and for every previewed method, to say why no person is asked in Go (or what the window does instead). touches is checked against the code, for the four kinds the walk knows (keychain, files, network, devices): a call graph of the Studio sources is walked from each method (bound_methods_derive_test.go), following every name of the package that a function mentions, package variables that hold functions, and any use of a sink package's name (a call, a function value, a package client such as http.DefaultClient); a sink that the method can reach and the entry does not list fails the test. An entry may list more. The sinks are listed at the top of that file. What the walk does not see, so touches can still understate there: a function value or an interface that is assigned inside another function (only package variables are followed), a method called on a value that is not named like a function of the package, calls through reflection, a package that is not a listed sink (the Wails runtime, os/signal, the standard library's other file and network calls), the runner functions other than New and NewExecutor, and what a sink package does beyond the functions listed for it. automationInternal: the unexported methods the automation endpoint reaches, which are not bound but are what a script that holds its token can do.

methods.does: The chat header's line (provider and model), made from the workspace's probe.yaml and the keychain's saved key (the key is read to know whether one is set, never shown).
The chat header's line in three parts for the header, made from the same settings as AIChatLabel (probe.yaml and the keychain's saved key).
Allows requests to one host:port for the rest of the session, at the strength CheckTarget showed.
methods.decision: Previewed, not asked: Go requires an earlier CheckTarget for the host and refuses an address that is never allowed, but nothing in Go asks a person. The window shows where the host leads and asks before it calls AllowHost; a bridge-token script can call CheckTarget and AllowHost itself.

methods.does: The window's answer to a pending confirmation (clear data, a send); counts only for the request with that id.
Changes one setting (language, dark mode, ...) on the connected device.
Builds the step lines for a request typed in the panel; reads nothing and writes nothing.
Says whether a finished run's report exists and no run is going.
Stops the run in progress.
Sends a conversation, the open file and (when their switches are on) the last run and the widget tree to the provider the workspace configures, after the outbound gate (redaction and bounds).
methods.decision: Decided: no confirmation in Go. The window asks before the first send to a destination it has not confirmed (confirmFirstChatSend, after PreviewAIChat shows the text and where it goes); nothing in Go ties a send to a preview, so a script with the bridge token can call Chat without one, as it can ExplainLastRun. The same gap the AI plan already records for Explain; closing it is a product decision, not made here.

methods.does: Says whether a suggestion may replace the failed step's line in the text the window holds; reads nothing from disk and writes nothing.

Says whether the rule-based fix of a failed see or tap may be inserted above it in the text the window holds: only while that text is the text the run read; reads nothing from disk and writes nothing.
Says where a request to a URL would go and whether its host is allowed yet; looks the name up.
methods.decision: Looks the name up and reports where a request would go; it sends no request and no content.

methods.does: Closes the workspace a person opened: it does what SetWorkspace does with no folder (so the reads and writes of the old folder stop being allowed) but only in memory, which is why touches is empty; refused while a run or a recording is going, checked under the run slot's lock and the state lock together with the change; a run takes the slot and its workspace under the same two locks, so one of the two wins. A connection that exists is not dropped.
Connects to a simulator, emulator or USB device and its agent (forwards a port, reads the token).
Connects to an agent by address, port and a token that was typed or given.
Connects to an agent with the token saved in the keychain for a device name; the token never reaches the window.
Removes the stored AI API key from the keychain.
One line about why Android devices may be missing (adb not found); looks for adb.
Closes the agent connection and its port forwards.
Says whether an explanation can be offered for the last run's failure.
Asks the AI provider for advice on each failed test of the last run.
methods.decision: Decided: no confirmation in Go; the window shows the preview of a hosted destination first and sends through ExplainPreviewed, which rechecks the destination. ExplainLastRun is the unpreviewed form, still bound (the same gap as Chat).

methods.does: Sends the explain request the person previewed, only to the destination the preview showed.
methods.decision: Previewed, not asked: Go compares the destination label it is given with the current one and stops on a mismatch (no preview has to have happened first); nothing in Go asks a person. The window shows the preview of a hosted destination first.

methods.does: Saves the last run's results as JSON or JUnit to a path chosen in a native dialog.
Asks the machine's own model server which models it has.
methods.decision: Asks model servers on this machine (loopback only) which models they have and sends no workspace content, so there is nothing to confirm.

methods.does: Sends an HTTP request to a host that was allowed; returns the answer redacted.
methods.decision: Previewed, not asked: Go refuses a host that was not allowed (AllowHost, at the strength CheckTarget showed), but nothing in Go asks a person; a bridge-token script can run CheckTarget, AllowHost and SendRequest without a window question. The window asks before AllowHost.

methods.decision: Listens for agents that announce themselves on the local network (mDNS) and sends no workspace content; a found device is never connected to or sent a token without ConnectWiFi or ConnectWiFiSaved, the second of which asks.

Whether a WiFi token is saved for a device name; never returns it.

automationInternal.does: Starts a run of a .probe file inside the automation roots on the connected device (the endpoint's run_file). A step `clear app data` reaches the same gate as a run from the window: it asks the window, and without a window it is not run; the person's own setting for simulators and emulators can answer it without asking.
The folders the endpoint may read, list, open and run from: the workspace a person opened, PROBE_STUDIO_WORKSPACE and PROBE_STUDIO_AUTOMATION_ROOTS.
Opens a workspace for the endpoint's open_workspace without widening the roots the endpoint may touch.
